title: CRLR/5/2013 of SMT. PRASANNA DEVI AND ORS Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND AND ANR

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Criminal Revision No. 05 of 2013
Smt. Prasanna Devi & others Ö Petitioners
Vs

State of Uttarakhand & another Ö Respondents
Mr. Anil Dabral, Advocate, present for the petitioners.
Mr. V.K. Jemeni, learned Deputy Advocate General, present for the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Lokendra Dobhal, Advocate, present for respondent No. 2.
Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral)
1. In this case, the First Information Report was filed
by respondent No. 2 ñ Smt. Sapna under Sections
315/323/498-A/506 of I.P.C. implicating the present
revisionists. Although, the learned Sessions Judge exonerated
the revisionist Nos. 1 and 2, who are the mother-in-law and
father-in-law of the complainant, for the offence under Section
315 of I.P.C. The learned Sessions Judge, before whom the
discharge application was filed, has come to the conclusion
that as far as Section 315 of I.P.C. is concerned, there is prima
facie evidence against the husband/revisionist No. 3. The
court has framed the charges under Section 228 of Cr.P.C.
against the revisionists. The charges were framed against the
revisionists under Sections 323/324/498-A/506 of I.P.C. and
Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act against the revisionists and
apart from the above offences the revisionist No. 3 has also
been charged under Section 315 of I.P.C.
2. There are various arguments which are being raised
by the learned counsel for the revisionist before this Court,
such as the FIR was belatedly lodged by the complainant and
there is no evidence for the offence under Section 315 of I.P.C.
against the husband/revisionist No. 3 and it is being argued
that based on the evidence of the prosecution, the case should
not be proceeded against the present revisionists.
3. At this stage, it would not be proper to make any
interference of this Court, more particularly, considering the

2
fact that all the revisionists are on bail. Nevertheless the
revision stands disposed with a direction that the court below
shall expedite the proceedings in the matter, after applying its
mind to the available evidence on record and hearing
submission of the respective counsels as well as considering
the case of the revisionist must proceed in accordance with
law, the Interim order dated 04.01.2013 stands vacated.
(Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.)
02.09.2015
Aswal
